page.layout: One block of verse in the centre of the page, set in italic type, with stanza indents; below it at the right a catchword-like signature "Et". No margin notes, no page number, no running head.

main_text.p:
Sex turmae, totidemque Duces, hos tota sequuntur
Agmina, tercentum Hispanae robora pubis
Cuique merent numero pedites, quorum vna cauato
Liuentis plumbi glandes intorquet ab aere
Seruatumque ignem fumanti infomite gestat.
Altera pars humeros ingentibus ingrauat haftis,
Omnibus in morem crines premit aerea cassis,
Omnibus it collo candentis circulus aeris
Sutilis, & gladius laeuum latus armat Iberus.

Iamque in conspectu varijs legio omnis in armis
Regis adest, dant signa tubae, quassataque fracto
Tympana tenta tonant strepitu, sedet altus, & omnes
Dux legit, instructasque acies animosque paratos,
Et tam certa Ducum mirari pectora gaudet.

Tu modo quae veterum monumenta insignia rerum
Ad seruas, nigrique e faucibus eripis orci
Liuida ne nomen seclorum obliteret aetas,
Tu mihi fama globos equitum, peditumque maniplos
Suggere, quique Duces externa in bella sequuti
Magnanimos ausus, cunctamque ex ordine gentem,
Non ego res tenebris possim, terraque latentes
Eruere, & coeli nitidas efferre sub auras
Tu mecum ingentis ni facti euoluueris oras.

Primus adest Buylus tales cui vestis admos
Vndique nigra fluit quo non magis vtilis alter
Veracis fidei ad vultum & pietatis amorem
Ore ciere viros, moresque inhibere nocentes,

page.notes: The verse is set in italic; the long s is printed as f in places ("fracto", "eripis") and is transcribed as printed. Some words are doubtful: "infomite" and "admos" may be misprints for "infomite" and "admos" as printed; "Buylus" read as printed. The final "Et" at the right is a catchword.
